info.bio:
Nelly se dio a conocer ante el público en el 2000 con el álbum Country Grammar, con el que arrasó las listas de todo el país. Con St. Lunatics, grabó en 2001 el álbum Free City. Su siguiente álbum, Nellyville, en 2002, le consagró como uno de los raperos más populares del momento, arrollando una vez más en ventas.

En 2002, el single "Hot In Herre" fue tremendamente popular, seguido de "Dilemma", con la colaboración de Kelly Rowland. Ese año se llevó dos premios Grammy.

scenes.name: Nelly y los St. Lunatics
scenes.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
scenes.author: Jonathan Abrams
scenes.desc: Ningún rapero de St. Louis había llegado al gran público; los St. Lunatics (Murphy Lee, Ali, Kyjuan, City Spud, Slo’ Down) tuvieron éxito regional con «Gimme What U Got» (1997) y, sin contrato de grupo, empujaron a Nelly en solitario a Universal. Country Grammar (2000), producido casi entero por Jay E en un estudio de una pista de patinaje donde no se podía fumar, fue número 1 más de un mes: sing-alongs de pop-rap con acento del Medio Oeste, el canto que heredaría Drake.

scenes.name: Dirty south
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.author: Javier Blánquez (ed.)
scenes.desc: La descentralización del poder del rap: Master P construye un imperio en Nueva Orleans, Jermaine Dupri en Atlanta, OutKast debuta en 1994 y Cash Money vende con facilidad en el sur (Nelly, Hot Boys, Mystikal, Jagged Edge).

mentions.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
mentions.author: Jonathan Abrams
mentions.text: …and Chicago’s Kanye West. Each added their unique imprint to hip-hop music that penetrated the mainstream— Eminem through his ability to provoke, Nelly through his Midwestern twang, and West through his relatable lyrics and fine-tuned production. Until those artists emerged, most Midwestern hip-hop…

mentions.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
mentions.author: Jonathan Abrams
mentions.text: …What U Got.” But no mainstream rappers had emerged from St. Louis, and the St. Lunatics had trouble securing a group deal. Instead, they pushed Nelly, born Cornell Haynes, to the forefront as a solo artist in helping him land a deal with Universal Music Group. Nelly dropped his studio debut album, Country Grammar, in June 2000. Jason “Jay E” Epperson handled the bulk of the production, and the St. Lunatics were…

mentions.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
mentions.author: Jonathan Abrams
mentions.text: …Up.” Country Grammar topped the U.S. Billboard 200 chart for more than a month. Jay E (producer, St. Louis): We always would give the beats to Nelly and the Lunatics. Sometimes we would go through beats, and they would write stuff then and there, but they were heavy smokers, and the skating-rink…

mentions.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
mentions.author: Jonathan Abrams
mentions.text: …they would go off and write in the car or whatever. Then they would come back, and we would do the songs that they wrote to them. I just remembered Nelly really loved [the “Country Grammar” track] and pretty much made that his song. Nelly was part of that new culture of hip-hop of where, to me, it kind of birthed a lot of rappers today with the singsongy sound. Even Drake, I feel like, has a lot of Nelly influence in his stuff.

mentions.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
mentions.author: Javier Blánquez (ed.)
mentions.text: …y por el camino se ha ido convirtiendo en un entretenimiento pop de éxito que ha dado productos arrolladores, aunque con fecha de caducidad, como Nelly en sus primeros años, y otros absolutamente atroces como Flo.Rida o Soulja Boy, considerados por los puristas del hip hop como payasadas…

mentions.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
mentions.author: Javier Blánquez (ed.)
mentions.text: …aire fresco. OutKast habían cambiado las reglas y la mentalidad del sur, y tras su estela emergieron las nuevas estrellas del dirty south —Ludacris, Nelly, Juvenile, T.I.—, a quienes se les había abonado el camino para causar un impacto en el mercado nacional con su propio lenguaje, es decir, la…

mentions.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
mentions.author: Javier Blánquez (ed.)
mentions.text: …y éxitos tan efímeros como pegadizos. Uno de los primeros ejemplos lo encontramos en «Hot in Herre», producción rompecaderas de The Neptunes para Nelly —el chico de póster surgido de la floreciente escena rap de Saint Louis, y que fue al star system negro lo que Justin Timberlake al blanco— cuyo…

mentions.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
mentions.author: Javier Blánquez (ed.)
mentions.text: …de las variedades regionales y la red de conexiones entre estados vecinos, sino a partir de quien ostente la corona. Primero fueron Ludacris y Nelly, y cuando se pasó su momento, irrumpieron T.I. —un extraficante de drogas que ha alternado desde 2004 las listas de éxitos y

mentions.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
mentions.author: Javier Blánquez (ed.)
mentions.text: …ni compromiso, los textos son pura anemia lírica, el sexismo y el materialismo campan a sus anchas (hay un momento en el vídeo de «Tip Drill» de Nelly en el que este desliza una tarjeta de crédito dorada entre las nalgas de una mujer). Sin embargo, entre esa síntesis de nihilismo y filosofía…

mentions.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
mentions.author: Javier Blánquez (ed.)
mentions.text: …cinematográfica. O lo mismo podría decirse de Cash Money Millionaries, un sello afincado en el dirty south, una zona en expansión (del sur proceden Nelly, Hot Boys, Mystical, OutKast o Jagged Edge), que vende álbumes con suma facilidad en el mercado sureño. Asimismo, Dr. Dre, ya lejos de Death Row,…

podcast.title: Blanked at Major Categories (General)
podcast.body: Nelly was listed among prominent rap/hip-hop artists who have been "blanked" in major general field Grammy categories. "In addition to B, J, Kanye and Kendrick, major category nominees that have been blanked include MC Hammer, Coolio, TLC, Nelly, Eminem, Ludicrous, Lil Wayne and Missy Elliott."

podcast.title: Precedent for Self-Replacement at Number One
podcast.body: Nelly was one of the four acts (Elvis Presley, The Beatles, and Boys to Men) that Outcast followed in replacing themselves at number one on the Hot 100. Including acts who succeeded themselves in featured roles, Nelly was among the seven acts to achieve this feat. "They followed Elvis Presley, The Beatles, Boys to Men, and Nelly."

xref.title: Initial Producer for *I Do Not Want What I Haven't Got* (1990)
xref.body: Nellee Hooper was initially hired to produce Sinead O'Connor's second album, *I Do Not Want What I Haven't Got*. However, Sinead walked out after just two days, stating that they "couldn't get on together," leading to Chris Birkett taking over production. "Basically, the story is that they started off this album with another producer, Nelly Hooper. And the Shanade walked out after two days, they couldn't get on together."

xref.title: Plagiarism Accusations Regarding "Do It" (2006)
xref.body: Timbaland, as producer for Nelly Furtado's song "Do It" (2006), faced accusations of plagiarism due to its similarities to Jan Tempest Suni's "Asad Jazzed Evening." "Almost immediately, some people began to hear similarities between the song Do It and Sunni's Asad Jazzed Evening, which is when the accusations of plagiarism began to fly."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Plagiarism Accusations for "Do It" (2006)
xref.body: Nelly Furtado's song "Do It," released in June 2006 from her Timbaland-produced "Loose" album, immediately drew accusations of plagiarism due to its strong resemblance to Jan Tempest Suni's "Asad Jazzed Evening." "Almost immediately, some people began to hear similarities between the song Do It and Sunni's Asad Jazzed Evening, which is when the accusations of plagiarism began to fly."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Plagiarism Allegations Against Timbaland and Nelly Furtado (2006)
xref.body: Jan Tempest Suni's "Asad Jazzed Evening" (2000) became the basis for plagiarism accusations when Nelly Furtado's song "Do It," produced by Timbaland, was released in 2006 and sounded similar. "Almost immediately, some people began to hear similarities between the song Do It and Sunni's Asad Jazzed Evening, which is when the accusations of plagiarism began to fly."
